test_title: SSC CGL 2024 Tier-I Official Paper (Held On: 10 Sept, 2024 Shift 1)
subject: general
question:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. More children go to school than at any time in the past. But more children today are out of school than any time in the past.

B. But it is not enough to blame the high birth rate for this state of affairs.

C. Indeed, it can be reasonably argued that continued mass illiteracy is not the result but the cause of the high birth rate.

D. There are more literate people in India today than ever before. But there are also more illiterates than ever before.
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The paragraph** begins **by introducing the central concept of literacy and illiteracy in India, setting a contrasting tone regarding the existence of both more literate and illiterate people today: **Sentence D**.
 
• **Sentence A** follows,** providing** a specific example of the paradoxical situation in today's context, more children attending school yet also more children out of school: "More children go to school than at any time in the past. But more children today are out of school than any time in the past."
 
• **Sentence B** **continues **by stating that it is not sufficient to blame only the high birth rate for this situation: "But it is not enough to blame the high birth rate for this state of affairs."
 
• **Sentence C** **concludes** the argument by presenting the idea that illiteracy may actually be the cause of the high birth rate rather than the effect: "Indeed, it can be reasonably argued that continued mass illiteracy is not the result but the cause of the high birth rate."

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Rearranged Paragraph:** *"There are more literate people in India today than ever before. But there are also more illiterates than ever before. More children go to school than at any time in the past. But more children today are out of school than any time in the past. But it is not enough to blame the high birth rate for this state of affairs. Indeed, it can be reasonably argued that continued mass illiteracy is not the result but the cause of the high birth rate."*
